caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 27 of 1980
lawyer:
Mr. Marfat Ali---For the Appellant. 
Mr. Moazzem Hossain, D.A.G---For the respondent.
parties:
Fazlur Rahman ------ Appellant.
Versus
People's Republic of Bangladesh ------Respondent.
full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff Fazlur Rahman filed the suit for declaration on his tenancy right under the government in respect of the land measuring 20.41 acres described in schedule A to the plaint with the averment, inter alia. that his father took settlement of the land described in schedule B to the plaint measuring 0.83 acres at a rental of Tk. 1-1-0 on the basis of a chit, Ext. 1 dated 12 Falgoon. 1350 B.S. and that he (plaintiff) got settlement from the ex-land-lords Ranjit Singh Nahar and others of the land described in schedule A to the plaint measuring 20.41 acres at a rental of Tk. 14/0 on the basis of a chit. Ext. 1 (a) dated 15 Chaitra, 1352 B.S. The two jamas were subsequently amalgamated and the plaintiff paid rent to the government on the basis of the amalgamated jama of Tk. 5/1/1. Plaintiff claims to have made the land fit for cultivation by removing bushes at a cost ranging between Tk. 15,000/-and 20.000/- and the P.R.R. and S.A. Khatians were duly prepared in his name. The plaintiff has been in peaceful enjoyment and possession of the land on payment of rent to the government. Curiously the plaintiff received a notice from the Government Tahasildar to appear before him with papers relating to the suit land. Accordingly he appeared before the Tahasildar and showed Government Dakhilas and Khatians but the Tahasildar asked the plaintiff to come again with papers of the sheriata of the ex-landlords. This time the plaintiff did not go to the Tahasildar who reported the matter to the C.O. (Rev). The plaintiff was directed to appear before the C.O. (Rev) with relevant papers. The plaintiff did not go to the C.O. (Rev) and the matter was subsequently reported to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), who asked the plaintiff to appear with necessary papers in respect of the suit property. The plaintiff appeared with all necessary papers before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) who gave the finding that the alleged pattan of the plaintiff from the ex-landlords was concocted and that all his papers relating to the settlement are fabricated and forged. though the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) accepted the pattan of plaintiff's father as genuine, he found over writing the Resister-II and other papers of the Revenue Office with the observation that these were concocted and forged showing false amalgamation of plaintiffs father's pattan with his alleged pattan relating to the land of schedule A. This finding of the A.D.C. (Rev) has cast a cloud upon the title of the plaintiff to the suit land. The plaintiff has, therefore, filed the suit for declaration of his tenancy right under the government in respect of the land of schedule A measuring 20. 41 acres. 

 3. Defendant No. 1, People's Republic of Bangladesh and defendant No. 2, A.D.C. (Rev), contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. Their case, in brief, is that an area of 80.86 acres of land including the suit land belonged to Zaminders Ranjit Singh Nahar and others and the said lands were recorded in khatian No. 3 in mouza Nafanagar within P.S. Bochegeni in District Dinajpur. The said lands were sold in auction No. 26.4.63 in Certificate Case No. 22 of 1962-63 and was purchased by the Government, who got possession of the same. It is seated by the defendants that plain-tiffs father had a jama for 0.83 acre (schedule B land) at a rental of Tk.1/1-and the land was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs father in khatian No. 11. Plaintiffs father paid rent up to 1369 B.S. Subsequently in collusion with some employees of the Tahasil Office plaintiff caused overwriting in Karcha Book, changed the page of R.O.R. and Register-11 showing amalgamation of the jama of Tk. 1 /1- of Khatian No. 11 and made an amalgamated jama of Tk. 15/1/- in respect of the said land. The plaintiff has illegally tampered with P.R.R., R.O.R. and Karcha Book and other Registers and papers of the settlement offices and he did so in collusion with the employees of the Revenue Department. The defendants categorically assert that plaintiffs papers in respect of the land of schedule A to the plaint are forged concocted and vogue without creating any right, title and interest in his favour. The matter having been reported to the A.D.C. (Rev), he sent a notice to the plaintiff. Thereafter he perused the plaintiffs papers. examined Register-II and other relevant documents and registers of the Revenue Office and being satisfied about the forgery committed by the plaintiff in respect of the said amalgamated jama, under his order dated 8.9.77 restored plot Nos. 554, 694, 682, 500, 501. 474, 473, 472 and 544 to khatian No. 3 of the landlord by excluding the same from R.S. khatian No. 11 where these were entered through forgery and manipulation and maintained 0.83 in R. S. Khatian No. 11 in the name of the plaintiff. 

 7. It is not disputed that plaintiffs father Mashiruddin took settlement from the ex-Land-lords Ranjit Singh Nahar and others the land of schedule B measuring 0.83 acre at a rental of Tk. 1/1 /- recorded in R.S. khatian No. 11. The dispute centers round the alleged story of pattan by the plaintiff in respect of the land of schedule A measuring 20.41 acres on the basis of a chit. Ext. 1(a). bearing the date 15 Chaitra, 1352 B.S. Plaintiff has examined some witnesses in order to prove the story of settlement of the land of schedule A to the plaint. In his evidence as P.W.1 plaintiff Fazlur Rahman states that his father took pattan of 0.83 acre (schedule B) at a rental of Tk. 1/1/- on the basis of a chit and that he himself got settlement of 20.41 acres (schedule A) at a jama of Tk. 14/- and he has filed two chits said to have been granted by Narendra Chatarjee, Naib of the ex-landlord. Plaintiff himself was present when the said chit, Ext. 1 (a). was granted and he got settlement of the land of schedule A on the basis of this pattan. This witness has also filed 3 dakhilas and claims to have made the land fit for cultivation. P.W. 4 Serajul Haque states that he was a Tahasildar of the Zaminder and he states that Narendra Chatarjee, Nail) of the Zaminder, wrote the chit, dated 12 Falgoon, 1350 B.S. (Ext. l) in respect of 0.83 acre of land in the name of plaintiffs father and that the said Naib also wrote a chit. Ext. 1 (a), in respect of 20.41 acres at a jama of Tk. 14/-. P.W.4 Serajul Haque, wrote dakhila, Ext. 2(a), in respect of 0.83 acre of land in the name of plaintiffs father and also granted dakhila Ext. 2 in respect of 20.41 acres in the name of the plaintiff. P.W.4 further states that the dakhila, Ext. 2(b) in respect of 20.41 acres in the name of the plaintiff is in the handwriting of Bhupati Chowdhury, who was the Zamindar's Taltasildar before him. In cross-examination the defendants challenged that P.W.4 Serajul Haque was in the employment of the Jamindar as a Tahasildar or that Bhupati Chowdhury was ever employed by the Zamindar as a Tahasildar. It was further challenged in the cross-examination of this witness that Narendra Chataijee was employed as Naib. P.W.4 has, in fact, failed to show any paper or document showing that he was the landlord's Tahasildar at any time or that Bhupati or Narendra Chatarjee were ever employed by the landlords as a Tahasildar or Naib. The other witnesses supporting the plaintiffs story of settlement is P.W.5 Kalu Mohammad who claims to have been present at the time of taking of pattan by the plaintiff. In his cross-examination, P.W.5 Kalu Mohammad states that he cannot say the plot number or area of the suit land. He claims that he went to the landlord's Sheresta in the morning by train but he can-not say the time of the train. The learned Deputy Attorney General has challenged the veracity of these two witnesses to supporting plaintiffs story of pattan from the Zamindar. There is no doubt that these two witnesses, P.W.4 and P.W.5. have not been able to prove plaintiffs story of pattan satisfactorily. 

 9. Before the trial court the defendants filed a number of documents. These are Ext. E an order sheet of certificate Case No. 22/62-63, Ext. F certificate of public demand. Exts. G and G(1). notices of the certificate case, Ext. H sale proclamation. Ext I certificate of sale, Ext J order of delivery of possession and other papers in support of the defendant's story about an auction sale of the suit land for default in payment of rent in Certificate Case No 22 of 1962-63. It is the case of the defendants that the auction' sale took place on 26.4.63 followed by delivery of possession in favour of the auction purchaser, namely, the government and subsequent settlement in favor of a number of borga tenants, namely Kafiluddin Abdul Matin and Kudratullah. The sole witness of the defendant, D.W.1 Government Tahasildar Abdul Latif Sarker has spoken about borga settlement to different persons. Unfortunately the exhibits filed on behalf of the defendants before the trial court were not filed before us for consideration and the list of documents shows that the Government pleader received back those documents on 26.7.79 on condition of filing the same, if necessary. Though the appeal was filed on 22.8.79, long after 13 years these exhibited documents, taken back on condition of refiling, have not been filed before this court. The learned Deputy Attorney General has found it to difficult to say as to why these documents have not been filed before this court. The learned Subordinate Judge has rightly observed that a plaintiff does not succeed on the weakness of the case of the defendant but he must succeed on the merit of his own case. 

 10. The learned Deputy Attorney General has contended that if the story of plaintiffs pattan had been true, there would have been payment of rent from 1956 to 1975. In fact, no evidence of payment of rent is coining before us during this long span of 18 years in support of plaintiffs story of settlement in respect of the land of schedule A to the plaint. 

 11. Ext. 4(a) is certified copy of an order dated 8.9.77 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Dinajpur, in case No. 71/27 of 1976-77 under rule 23(4) of the Tenancy Rules made under section 152 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950. The present plaintiff was opposite party in this proceeding and he filed his pattani papers including dakhilas alleged to have been granted by the ex-landlords. In his order the A.D.C. (Rev) mentions that the first set of dakhilas showing settlement of 0.83 acres at a rental of Tk.1.06 by the ex-landlord appears to be genuine, but the second set of dakhilas showing settlement of 20.14 acres at a rental of Tk.14/- appears to be forged and produced recently. On examination the A.D.C. (Rev) found that S.A. Khatian No. 11 in respect of 0.83 acre of land was rightly recorded in favour of the opposite party but subsequently through manipulation 20.14 acres of land of different plots were brought into that khatian by increasing the rent to Tk. 15/-. On examination by the A.D.C (Rev). Registrar-II showed signs of manipulation by overwriting. The P.R.R. and Tahasil the copy of S.A. Khatian were examined and it was found that nine plots of khas land were included in Khatian No. 11 with different ink. It was further noted that though the opposite party (present plaintiff) paid rent for the khatian at the rate of Tk. 1.06 up to 1369 B.S. yet after this manipulation rent was again realised from him for the same holding from 1367 B.S. to 1370 B.S. On examination of the Office copy of the S.A. khatian of the C.O. (Rev) it was found that vanishing ink was used to erase those plots from the khas khatian and that handwriting of khatian No. 11 (disputed khatian) was entirely different from the handwriting of khatian Nos. 10 and 12. The A.D.C. (Rev) found Khatian No. 11 in the name of the opposite party (present plaintiff) which contains 0.83 acre at a rental of 11.1.06 but subsequently through fraud khas land measuring 20.14 acres of 9 plots were brought in Khatian No. 11 and accordingly plot Nos. 554, 694. 682. 500, 501, 474, 473, 472 and 554 fraudulently entered into khatian No. 11 were restored to Khatian No. 3 maintaining 0.83 acre of land in the name of the plaintiff in khatian No. 11 under rule 23 (4) the State Acquisition Rule. Under rule 23(4) the Revenue Officer is empowered to direct excision of fraudulent entry from the record of rights after final publication there of after consulting the previous settlement records, preliminary rent-rolls, draft record-of-rights. tahasil copies of records and Register-II. 

 13. Plaintiff has examined a number of witnesses to show his possession in the suit land. The plaintiff as P.W.1 states that after taking settlement he invested a lot of money running between Tk. 15,000/- to 20,000/- for removing bushes and making the land fit for cultivation. P.W.2 Haji Salah Mohammad supporting plaintiffs possession for 30 years in his relation. P.W.3 Kashiruddin has supported plaintiffs possession in the suit land for a period of 30/35 years. In cross-examination he can neither say about the area of the suit plots nor about their location from nearby the river. P.W.5 Kalu Mohammad speaks about plaintiffs possession for 30/35 years without any knowledge about the plot Nos. or area of the suit land. The other witness supporting the plaintiffs possession is P.W.6 Sakibuddin. He says that the plaintiff has been in possession for a long time. In cross-examination he states that there is a case against him in the Court of A.D.C. in respect of Government land and that an eviction case is pending against him. Evidently this witness is not a disinterested witness. In fact, no impartial or reliable evidence has come to support plaintiffs possession. P.W. 1 examined on behalf of the Government is a Tahasildar of Local Tahasil Office and he states that he served a notice upon the plaintiff to produce necessary papers, but the plaintiff did not appear before him. Thereafter he reported the matter to C.O. (Rev) and from there the matter was reported to A.D.C. (Rev) and, after getting notice, the plaintiff produced his papers. The A.D.C. examined all relevant papers and dakhilas and passed an order dated 8.9.77 restoring plot Nos. 554, 694, 682, 500, 501, 474, 473, 472 and 544 to khatian No. 3 of the landlord by excluding the same from R. S. Khatian No. 11 where these were entered through forgery and manipulation and maintaining 0.83 acre in R.S. khatian No. 11 in the name of the plaintiff. D.W. 1 states about auction-sale of the suit property on 26.4.63 in Certificate Case No. 22 of 1962-63. This witness states that the Government took delivery of possession and thereafter the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) under his order dated 8.9.77 set aside the fraudulent pattan of the plaintiff in respect of the land of schedule A and the Government took delivery of possession on 2.12.77 by beat of drum in the locality. Thereafter the Government gave settlement to different persons including Kafiluddin, Abdul Matin and Kudratullah. The learned Advocate for the appellant has relied on the judgment passed in the criminal case being T.R. Case No. 1269 of 1977 under section 379 of Penal Code in support of plaintiffs possession in the suit land. The learned Deputy Attorney General has, on the other hand, sub-mitted that this being a government khas land limitation of 60 years will apply to this case and the story of plaintiffs pattan cannot stretch beyond 1352 B.S. We find enough substance in the contention of the learned Deputy Attorney General.
